newsitem.title: INDONESIA: East Timor rebel leader dies after armed contact.
newsitem.headline: East Timor rebel leader dies after armed contact.

text.p: Indonesia's military said on Thursday that a key East Timorese rebel leader had been captured after a gunbattle in the former Portuguese colony but had died of gunshot wounds.

East Timor military commander Colonel Slamat Sidabutar told Reuters by telephone from the capital of Dili that David Alex died on Wednesday night after was flown to that provincial city for treatment.
He had been captured earlier after a confrontation near the second city of Baucau, about 100 km (62 miles) to the east.
"It's not true that he died in custody, but he died while he was being treated and was receiving a blood transfusion. Doctors tried to treat him, but he had lost too much blood," Sidabutar said.
Sidabutar said Alex had two large bullet wounds received in shooting between rebels and locally raised troops of the Indonesian army.

Alex was believed to be the second in command of about 200 guerrillas from the military wing of the pro-independence Fretilin party, which has opposed Indonesia's rule in East Timor since Jakarta's 1975 invasaion.
"He was a rebel leader who was sought because he was part of a group that had killed members of the community," he said.
Sidabutar declined to give any further information.
At least 35 people have died in various clashes in East Timor since late May, when Indonesia held its general election. Seventeen security force members died in one attack.
The United Nations does not recognise Indonesia's 1976 declaration of East Timor as its 27th province. The U.N. regards Portugal as the administering power.
